n: Before promising restoration to Israel’s mountains (ch. 36), God pronounces judgment on Mount Seir—Edom—which hoped to seize Israel’s land.

f.w: Moreover the word of the LORD came unto me

n: Ezekiel turns his face against Mount Seir, the mountainous homeland of Edom, south of the Dead Sea.

f.g: The highlands of Edom, home of Esau’s descendants.

n: God is against Seir and will stretch out his hand to make it utterly desolate.

f.w: I will stretch out mine hand against thee

n: Edom’s towns will be ruined, and it will know the Lord.

f.w: I will lay thy cities waste

n: Edom nursed an ancient, endless hatred—going back to Jacob and Esau—and attacked Israel at its lowest moment, when Jerusalem fell.

f.w: in the time of their calamity

n: Since Edom did not hate bloodshed, bloodshed will pursue it. A play on words: Edom (’edom) and blood (dam) sound alike in Hebrew.

f.g: A pun on Edom’s name and the Hebrew for blood.

n: Seir will become so desolate that no one comes or goes.

f.w: him that passeth out and him that returneth

n: Its hills, valleys, and ravines will be filled with the slain.

f.w: I will fill his mountains with his slain men

n: Edom will be a permanent ruin. Historically, the Edomites were pushed out of their homeland by Arab tribes (the Nabateans) and later absorbed into Judea; Edom as a nation disappeared.

f.w: I will make thee perpetual desolations

n: Edom boasted that both nations—Israel and Judah—would become its property. But it forgot that the Lord was there. The land belongs to God.

f.w: These two nations and these two countries shall be mine
f.g: The former northern and southern kingdoms.

n: God will repay Edom according to its own anger and envy, and make himself known through that judgment.
God heard every insult Edom spoke about Israel’s mountains: “They are desolate—ours to devour!”

f.w: I have heard all thy blasphemies

n: In boasting against Israel, Edom was really boasting against God, and he heard it all.

f.w: with your mouth ye have boasted against me

n: While the whole earth rejoices, Edom will be desolate.

f.g: Possibly “as the whole earth rejoiced (at your fall).”

n: As Edom rejoiced over Israel’s ruin, so it will be ruined—a principle of measure-for-measure justice. Then Ezekiel turns, in chapter 36, to the restoration of Israel’s mountains.
